newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil meat producers' earnings seen hurt in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Brazil meat producers' earnings seen hurt in 1996.

text.p: Brazil's meat producers will perform worse-than-expected this year due to an oversupply in the local market and sharply higher soy prices, Credit Lyonnais Securities said in a report.

Credit Lyonnais said it was reducing its earnings estimates for the Brazilian meat sector for both this year and next due to poor expectations for the third quarter and projected slow growth in consumer demand in 1997.
But the sector's financial picture should brighten in the medium term as cost pressures ease in late 1997 and consumer demand increases in 1988, it said.
Credit Lyonnais said the Brazilian grain harvest is expected to be bountiful in 1997, but removal of the ICMS tax on exports should cause cost pressure through 1997.
Nonetheless, in the long run, companies in the sector will benefit from lower port costs and elimination of export taxes as the government moves to reduce the so-called "Brazil cost," it said.
